o: Write and run a short program whose instructions execute in sequence.
Use input() to store a response in a named variable.
Use print() to display stored values and trace the exact output.
c: A program follows instructions in order. In a club-name program, obtain the input before attempting to display the stored value.
input("Club name?") asks the user for text. Store the answer with club = input("Club name?"). The question itself is not the stored answer.
print(club) displays the value held in club. print("club") instead prints the literal word club; quotation marks change the meaning.
Predict the output using a sample response, write the short program, test two inputs in the ERL interpreter, then check and improve any mistakes.

e:
WRITE CODE [3 marks]
A school club wants to ask for a pupil’s chosen team and then display the team name. Write TWO lines of OCR ERL to do this. Use the variable team.

team = input("Team?") [2: correct input() and assignment]
print(team) [1]
A valid alternative prompt is acceptable.

TRACE CODE [2 marks]
The program is:
print("Welcome")
print("Goodbye")
State the two lines of output in the correct order.

Welcome [1]
Goodbye [1]
The instructions run in sequence, top to bottom.

DEBUG CODE [4 marks]
A student writes:
print(team)
team = input("Team?")
Explain why the program is incorrect and rewrite the two lines in a correct order.

The program tries to use team before it has been assigned a value [1]. Input must be obtained before output [1].
team = input("Team?") [1]
print(team) [1].
